clue.text: A fine fellow with capacity for good humour

parts.note: F is the standard abbreviation for fine, as on pencil leads
F is the abbreviation for fellow, as in FRS
capacity in the sense of competence or ability

explanation.surface: A decent sort of chap who can be relied on to keep everyone cheerful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' simply joins the pieces; the letters run A, F, F then ABILITY.
explanation.definitionFit: Affability is friendliness and geniality, which is what good humour describes in a person.

clue.text: Crinoline offered at fraction of old price, over a drink

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece over another means it comes first, above it

parts.note: a farthing was a quarter of an old British penny, a small fraction of a price
ale is a drink of beer

explanation.surface: A hooped skirt going cheap at a jumble sale, with a pint thrown in.
explanation.walkthrough: A farthing was the smallest pre-decimal British coin, a quarter of a penny. In a down answer 'over' puts FARTHING above ALE.
explanation.definitionFit: A farthingale was a hooped framework under a skirt, an earlier relative of the crinoline.

clue.text: Going round rings horrifies a horse

indicators.note: going round tells us one piece encircles the other, so a word is opened up to hold something

parts.note: to appal is to horrify
O looks like a ring, so two rings are two Os

explanation.surface: Someone circling a ring of jumps terrifies the horse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rings' is not jewellery or a circus ring: read it as letter shapes, which 'Going round' places inside the verb; the lone 'a' is added at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: The appaloosa is a spotted North American breed of riding horse.

clue.text: Absurd 'description of Dostoevsky hero

definitions.meaning: Prince Myshkin is the title character of Dostoevsky's novel The Idiot, so a word describing him is formed from that title

explanation.surface: A literary critic dismisses an adjective for a Russian novel's protagonist.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiotic means stupidly foolish, the same as absurd, and is also the adjective from the novel's title character.

clue.text: There's no support, apparently, for such a climb

definitions.text: There's no support, apparently, for such a climb

parts.words: There's no support, apparently, for such a climb
parts.note: a famous conjuring illusion in which a boy climbs a rope that stands rigidly upright with nothing holding it up

explanation.surface: A mountaineer frets that this ascent has no ropes or anchors.
explanation.definitionFit: The fabled Indian conjuror's feat has a rope rise into the air unaided for an assistant to climb, so it seems unsupported.

clue.text: What's paid in China to capture animal in part of Mexico

indicators.note: to capture means to take in and hold, so one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: the yuan is the currency of China
a cat is an animal

explanation.surface: Wages in China are spent catching a creature somewhere in Mexico.
explanation.definitionFit: Yucatan is a peninsula and state in south-east Mexico.

clue.text: Originator of courses, one dismissed by principal

indicators.note: dismissed means sent away, so a piece is removed from the word

parts.note: principal as an adjective or noun means chief
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A head teacher sacks the person who devised the curriculum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' is a link: CHIEF loses its I.
explanation.definitionFit: A cook devises and prepares the courses of a meal, so is their originator.

clue.text: Card obviously not concealed up one's sleeve

definitions.meaning: a playing card of the red suit marked with that symbol

definitions.text: obviously not concealed up one's sleeve
definitions.meaning: someone who wears their feelings openly is said to wear this on their sleeve, plainly in view rather than hidden

explanation.surface: A card trick where the card is plainly not hidden up the magician's sleeve.
explanation.definitionFit: A heart is a playing card, and the idiom of wearing one's heart on one's sleeve means showing emotions openly.

clue.text: It's ready for laying out in Luxembourg

definitions.text: It's ready for laying out in Luxembourg

parts.words: It's ready for laying out in Luxembourg
parts.note: ready is slang for cash and laying out is spending, so this is the money once spent in that country

explanation.surface: Something is prepared for being spread out in a small European duchy.
explanation.definitionFit: The franc was Luxembourg's currency before the euro, the cash a shopper there would spend.

clue.text: Degenerated, not initially having symbols of success

indicators.note: not initially means the opening letter of the word is lost

parts.note: to atrophy is to waste away or degenerate

explanation.surface: Something went downhill despite winning trophies at first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not initially' drops the first letter, A, from ATROPHIED.
explanation.definitionFit: Trophied means adorned with trophies, the cups and prizes that symbolise victory.

clue.text: Top commander ignoring new woman, a chirpy creature

indicators.note: ignoring means leaving out, so a letter is dropped from the word

parts.note: C-in-C, commander-in-chief, is the top military commander
Ada is a woman's name

explanation.surface: A general snubs a new female recruit, a cheerful sort.
explanation.walkthrough: C-in-C, commander-in-chief, is a common crossword abbreviation; the 'a' before the definition is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A cicada is an insect famous for its loud shrill chirping song.

clue.text: Bird seen around the French cowherd's hut

indicators.note: around means one piece goes about the other, holding it inside

parts.note: the chat is a small songbird such as the stonechat
le is French for the

explanation.surface: Birdwatchers spot a bird near a Frenchman's mountain shed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seen' is only a link; the chat is a songbird family, not conversation.
explanation.definitionFit: A chalet is originally a herdsman's hut in the Swiss Alps, used while cattle graze high pastures.

clue.text: At last, painter in garret is held to be cultivated

indicators.note: held means kept inside, so this word is placed within the attic
in means the painter's final letter goes inside the attic

parts.note: a garret is a room under the roof, an attic

indicators.note: at last asks for the final letter of the word painter

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Finally, a starving painter in his garret is considered refined.
explanation.walkthrough: 'garret' is not literal: it is ATTIC. R, the last of painter, goes 'in' it (ARTTIC) and IS is 'held' too, giving A-R-T-IS-TIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Artistic means having refined taste and appreciation of the arts, which is to be cultivated.

clue.text: At home, deep in thought about former partner's budget

indicators.note: about here means concerning, so the thoughtful state is about the ex, who comes first

parts.note: in means at home
an ex is a former partner
pensive means deep in thought

explanation.surface: Someone at home broods over an ex-partner's household finances.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' is used loosely: the thoughtfulness is about the ex, who comes first. 'budget' is an adjective here, not a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Budget used as an adjective, as in budget prices, means cheap.

clue.text: Some seen round old ruin

indicators.note: some means only part of the text is used, here a run of letters inside two words

explanation.surface: A few things are noticed around some old ruins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seen' is a link; the letters run across 'round old'.
explanation.definitionFit: To undo something is to wreck or bring it to ruin, as in 'his pride was his undoing'.

clue.text: Very serious fellow producing records

parts.note: chronic in British slang means very bad or serious
Les is a man's name, Leslie

explanation.surface: A gravely solemn man turns out documents.
explanation.definitionFit: Chronicles are historical records of events set down in order.

clue.text: Spanish gentleman given new role, supporting secret plot

indicators.note: in a down answer a supporting piece sits underneath the other

parts.note: a cabal is a secret group of plotters or their plot

indicators.note: new means the word role is made afresh in a different order

explanation.surface: An actor takes a fresh part as a Spanish don in a conspiracy drama.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges ROLE into LERO, which goes beneath CABAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Caballero is the Spanish for a gentleman or knight.

clue.text: In untidy pal's room a piano is out of place

indicators.note: in means the piano's letter is placed within the jumble
untidy means messed up, so these letters are thrown into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, with its s
taken as written
P is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly

explanation.surface: A piano wedged into a friend's cluttered room looks awkward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'untidy' scrambles PALSROOMA into MALAROPOS, and 'In' places P inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Malapropos means inappropriate or inopportune, not suited to the place or time.

clue.text: Unprincipled, like someone shot in the gallery?

definitions.text: like someone shot in the gallery?
definitions.meaning: a rogues' gallery is a police collection of mugshots, so a person photographed there is a rascal

explanation.surface: A dishonest figure gets shot at an art gallery.
explanation.definitionFit: Roguish means rascally and dishonest, and those in a rogues' gallery have been shot by a camera.

clue.text: How the chic are turned out, wasting no time

definitions.text: How the chic are turned out

explanation.surface: Fashionable folk dress quickly.
explanation.definitionFit: Smartly means both stylishly dressed and quickly or briskly.

clue.text: Rolls originally baked as afterthought

indicators.note: originally asks for the opening letters of the following words

parts.note: PS, postscript, is an afterthought added to a letter

explanation.surface: The bread rolls were baked only as an afterthought.
explanation.walkthrough: BAPS are soft bread rolls in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Baps are soft round bread rolls, a British term.

clue.text: Begged? Sir Percy Blakeney was bound to!

definitions.text: Sir Percy Blakeney was bound to!
definitions.meaning: the Scarlet Pimpernel was hunted everywhere, 'they seek him here, they seek him there', so he had to be looked for

explanation.surface: An exclamation that the Scarlet Pimpernel was bound to plead.
explanation.walkthrough: Sir Percy Blakeney is the Scarlet Pimpernel of Baroness Orczy's novels; split as two words the answer means 'be looked for'.
explanation.definitionFit: Besought is the past of beseech, meaning implored or pleaded.

clue.text: Prohibition gangster regarded as commonplace

parts.note: a ban is a prohibition
Al Capone was the famous Chicago gangster

explanation.surface: A Prohibition-era mobster seen as nothing special.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regarded as' is a link; capital-P Prohibition hints at Capone's era but here just means a ban.
explanation.definitionFit: Banal means trite and unoriginal, ordinary.

clue.text: Drawing of cuttlefish

definitions.meaning: a drawing done in brown cuttlefish ink
The cuttlefish genus, and the name of the animal's ink

explanation.definitionFit: Sepia names both the cuttlefish and the brown pigment from its ink, so also a picture made with it.

clue.text: Sick greeting from Cockney?

indicators.note: Cockney speakers famously drop the h at the start of words

parts.note: hailing someone is greeting them

explanation.surface: A Londoner calls out a hello to an unwell friend.
explanation.walkthrough: A Cockney is a working-class Londoner, whose accent drops initial H.
explanation.definitionFit: Ailing means unwell or sick.

clue.text: Asian accommodating English friend in Islington area

indicators.note: accommodating means providing room for, so other letters go inside

parts.note: N1 is the London postcode of Islington, with 1 read as I
a pal is a friend

explanation.surface: An Asian visitor puts up an English mate in north London.
explanation.walkthrough: Islington is a district of London whose postcode is N1; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A Nepali is a person from Nepal, in south Asia.

clue.text: Novel I printed, being very daring

indicators.note: novel means new, so these letters take a fresh order

explanation.surface: An author brags that the book they published was bold.
explanation.definitionFit: Intrepid means fearless and bold.

clue.text: The head made a bloomer?

definitions.meaning: use your ... means use your head, from rhyming slang ... of bread
a bloomer is a long crusty ... with slashes on top, so a baker made one

explanation.surface: The boss made a blunder.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a bloomer is a kind of bread, though it also means a blunder.
explanation.definitionFit: Loaf is rhyming-slang shorthand for head, and a bloomer is one kind of bread.

clue.text: If not reason, there's rhyme in this deception

definitions.text: If not reason, there's rhyme in this deception

parts.words: If not reason, there's rhyme in this deception
parts.note: plays on 'neither rhyme nor reason': the trickery's name is a rhyming jingle

explanation.surface: A con trick with a jingle but no logic.
explanation.definitionFit: Hokey-pokey means trickery or hocus-pocus, and its two halves rhyme.
